# apscp: Decision Support Tool for the Antarctic Peninsula

[![lifecycle](https://img.shields.io/badge/Lifecycle-stable-brightgreen.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html)
[![R-CMD-check-Ubuntu](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/jeffreyhanson/apscp/R-CMD-check-ubuntu.yaml?branch=master&label=Ubuntu)](https://github.com/jeffreyhanson/apscp/actions)
[![R-CMD-check-Windows](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/jeffreyhanson/apscp/R-CMD-check-windows.yaml?branch=master&label=Windows)](https://github.com/jeffreyhanson/apscp/actions)
[![Docker
Status](https://img.shields.io/docker/cloud/build/naturecons/wheretowork?label=Docker%20build)](https://hub.docker.com/r/naturecons/wheretowork)
[![Coverage
Status](https://codecov.io/github/jeffreyhanson/apscp/coverage.svg?branch=master)](https://codecov.io/github/jeffreyhanson/apscp?branch=master)

Interactive decision support tool to navigate management options for the
Antarctic Peninsula. The tool identifies priority areas for implementing
policies for conservation, tourism, and scientific research. To achieve
this, it leverages previously published data ([Lee et
al. 2024](https://doi.org/10.1007/s13280-024-02009-4)) and
multi-objective optimization techniques through the [*prioritizr*
package](https://prioritizr.net) ([Hanson et
al. 2025](https://doi.org/10.1111/cobi.14376)). Although default
parameters are specified based on stakeholder surveys, users can
calibrate weights and representation targets to fine tune optimization
procedures according to their own preferences. Optimization procedures
can be performed with the ‘Gurobi’ (<https://www.gurobi.com/>) or ‘CBC’
(via the ‘rcbc’ package, <https://github.com/dirkschumacher/rcbc>) exact
algorithm solvers.

## Contributing

The application is a [Shiny web
application](https://mastering-shiny.org/) developed using the [R
statistical computing environment](https://www.r-project.org/).
Specifically, it uses the [*golem*
framework](https://thinkr-open.github.io/golem/). This means that the
application is effectively an [R package](https://r-pkgs.org/) that
contains code for defining and launching the application ([see here for
more details](https://engineering-shiny.org/)). The R code files
(located in the `./R` directory) are organized using the following
naming conventions:

- `app_*`: Defines the web application:
  - `app_config.R`: Imports configuration settings.
  - `app_global.R`: Initializes the application. It performs a similar
    to the `global.R` file in typical Shiny applications.
  - `app_server.R`: Defines the (back-end) server-side logic for the
    application. It performs a similar role to the `server.R` file in
    typical Shiny applications.
  - `app_ui.R`: Defines the (font-end) user interface for the
    application. It performs a similar role to the `ui.R` file in
    typical Shiny applications.
- `server_*`: Defines components used to assemble the server-side logic
  for the application.
- `ui_`\*: Defines functions used to create user interface elements.
- `class_*`: Defines [*R6* object classes](https://r6.r-lib.org/) for
  managing data. used in the back-end of the application.
- `fct_*`: Defines functions for analysis and data manipulation.
- `widget_*`: Defines custom [*htmlwidgets*
  widgets](https://www.htmlwidgets.org/) for user interface used by the
  application.
- `utils_*`: Defines utility functions.

## Getting help

Thank you for checking out this application. If you encounter any
software defects (e.g. application crashes, unexpected behavior, or
spelling mistakes), please feel free to post them on the [issue
tracker](https://github.com/jeffreyhanson/apscp/issues).
